originality.rationale: The complete two-focus inradius and center phase diagram for all separation parameters was not found in targeted primary sources or published-finding corpus. The roots-of-unity model note already proves the s=1 numerical endpoint; this is acknowledged as covered. Geng–Qiu gives an asymptotic n problem; Rabinowitz gives Cassini shape and tangency facts; neither statement, alone or by a direct cited implication, supplies all-maximal-center classification or the universal quadratic lower bound. Classical uncatalogued incircle terminology remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: Classical Cassinian-oval geometry from nineteenth-century compendia may express the same largest-inscribed-circle profile under unfamiliar terminology.

value.rationale: A natural geometric invariant for the complete classical Cassini family, not an artificial slice: every separation and all inball centers have a closed formula. The optimizer bifurcation at the known convexity transition has a quantified square-root law and persists across subsequent topology changes. The same calculation settles the full finite-degree-two polynomial-lemniscate extremal problem with rigid equality. The result supplies an exact finite-degree benchmark for a recently solved asymptotic problem.
